questions.prompt: Which command lists the containers that are currently running?
options: docker ls
docker ps
docker list
docker containers
questions.explanation: docker ps lists running containers; add -a to include stopped ones.

questions.prompt: Which file describes the steps used to build a Docker image?
options: Dockerfile
docker-compose.yml
image.json
package.json
questions.explanation: A Dockerfile contains the instructions that docker build executes to produce an image.

questions.prompt: Which Dockerfile instruction sets the base image for a build?
options: BASE
IMAGE
FROM
START
questions.explanation: FROM names the base image (or stage) that subsequent instructions build on.

questions.prompt: Which command downloads an image from a registry without starting a container?
options: docker fetch
docker download
docker clone
docker pull
questions.explanation: docker pull fetches an image and its layers from a registry such as Docker Hub.

questions.prompt: What does "docker run -p 8080:80 nginx" do?
options: Maps port 8080 on the host to port 80 in the container
Maps port 80 on the host to port 8080 in the container
Limits the container to ports 80 and 8080
Runs nginx on both ports 8080 and 80 of the host
questions.explanation: The -p flag uses the format hostPort:containerPort.

questions.prompt: Which command asks a running container to shut down gracefully?
options: docker pause
docker stop
docker rm
docker inspect
questions.explanation: docker stop sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a grace period; docker pause only freezes processes.

questions.prompt: What is the relationship between a Docker image and a container?
options: An image is a running instance of a container
They are the same thing under two names
A container is a running instance of a read-only image
A container is a backup copy of an image
questions.explanation: Images are immutable templates; containers are created from them and add a writable layer.

questions.prompt: Which Dockerfile instruction provides a default command that is replaced when arguments are given to docker run?
options: RUN
EXPOSE
LABEL
CMD
questions.explanation: CMD sets the default command/arguments and is overridden by anything passed after the image name in docker run.

questions.prompt: Which capability does ADD have that COPY does not?
options: It can copy files from the build context
It automatically extracts a local tar archive into the destination
It can set the owner of copied files
It can copy files from an earlier build stage
questions.explanation: ADD unpacks recognized local tar archives (and can fetch URLs); COPY only copies files as they are.

questions.prompt: What does the EXPOSE instruction in a Dockerfile do?
options: Documents the port the container listens on without publishing it
Publishes the port on the host automatically
Opens the port in the host firewall
Forces the application to bind to that port
questions.explanation: EXPOSE is metadata; you still need -p or -P at run time to publish ports.

questions.prompt: A container uses a named volume. What happens to the volume data when the container is removed with docker rm?
options: It is deleted with the container
It is merged into the image
It persists until the volume is explicitly removed
It is pushed to the registry
questions.explanation: Named volumes have a lifecycle independent of containers; use docker volume rm to delete them.

questions.prompt: Which network driver is used by default for standalone containers on a single host?
options: host
bridge
overlay
none
questions.explanation: Containers join the default bridge network unless another network is specified.

questions.prompt: Which command starts all services defined in a Compose file in the background?
options: docker compose up -d
docker compose run --all
docker compose start --build
docker compose create -d
questions.explanation: up builds/creates/starts services; -d runs them detached.

questions.prompt: Which flag sets an environment variable inside a container at run time?
options: -p
-v
-e
-u
questions.explanation: docker run -e KEY=value sets an environment variable; -p publishes ports, -v mounts volumes, -u sets the user.

questions.prompt: In a Node.js Dockerfile, why is package.json copied and npm install run before copying the rest of the source?
options: Because npm install cannot read files copied later
To make the final image smaller by deduplicating files
Because COPY . . would otherwise skip package.json
So the dependency layer stays cached until package.json changes
questions.explanation: Layer caching invalidates a layer and all later ones when its inputs change; keeping dependencies first avoids reinstalling on every code change.

questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of a multi-stage build?
options: The final image contains only the artifacts needed at runtime, not the build toolchain
Stages build in parallel on separate hosts
Each stage shares a writable layer with the others
It lets one image run multiple processes safely
questions.explanation: You compile in one stage and COPY --from the result into a slim final stage, so compilers and sources are left out.

questions.prompt: Why can containers on a user-defined bridge network reach each other by container name, while the default bridge network cannot?
options: The default bridge blocks all container-to-container traffic
User-defined bridges provide automatic DNS resolution of container names
User-defined bridges assign the same IP to all containers
Names are resolved through the host /etc/hosts file only
questions.explanation: Docker's embedded DNS server resolves container and service names on user-defined networks; the legacy default bridge needs IPs or --link.

questions.prompt: A Dockerfile uses ENTRYPOINT in shell form (ENTRYPOINT node app.js). What is a likely consequence when running docker stop?
options: The container cannot start because shell form is invalid
The app receives SIGKILL immediately without a grace period
The app runs twice, once under the shell and once directly
The shell is PID 1 and the app may not receive SIGTERM, so it gets killed after the timeout
questions.explanation: Shell form wraps the command in /bin/sh -c, so signals go to the shell; exec form makes the app PID 1 and lets it handle SIGTERM.

questions.prompt: A RUN step downloads a 500 MB file, and a later RUN step deletes it. What happens to the final image size?
options: It still includes the 500 MB, because the earlier layer is immutable
It shrinks, because deleting removes the data from all layers
It shrinks only if the image is built with --squash by default
It grows slightly because the deletion layer duplicates the data
questions.explanation: Layers are additive; a delete only masks the file in a later layer. Delete in the same RUN step or use multi-stage builds.

questions.prompt: When a container modifies a file that comes from a read-only image layer, what happens?
options: The image layer is modified in place for all containers
The container fails with a read-only filesystem error
The file is copied up into the container's writable layer and modified there
The change is written to a new image layer automatically
questions.explanation: Union filesystems use copy-on-write; the original image layer remains unchanged and other containers are unaffected.

questions.prompt: On Linux, what is the effect of "-p 8080:80" when a container runs with --network host?
options: Traffic is routed through NAT to the mapped port
The container gets a second network interface
Docker refuses to start the container
Port mappings are ignored because the container uses the host network stack directly
questions.explanation: With host networking there is no network namespace isolation or NAT, so the app binds to host ports itself and -p has no effect.
